name: UI Animation / Product Motion Design
visualIdentity: Commercial product motion built around accurate interfaces, real copy, and established branding. Separate cards, charts, numbers, and states into animatable elements; explain features through causal changes, shared elements, and precise framing.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to product feature demos and launches. Also suitable for explanatory or interactive product tours with state toggles, keyboard navigation, and accessible diagram or network panels. Scroll stories, carousels, or galleries are optional patterns only when their content fits.
limitations: Avoid invented interfaces and repeatedly sliding whole screenshots. Keep labels, controls, provenance, comparisons, and essential copy visible. Use exploded reveals only for separable components whose relationships matter; use galleries only for actual images and captions. Do not imply working playback without audio assets.
palette: No intrinsic palette is specified. Product UI, brand colors, approved references, existing semantic mappings, and source artwork retain their exact colors and roles. Optional fallback colors for new presentation elements only: background #F7F9FA and foreground #263440; no gradients. Check contrast on composed frames; do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast.
motionAndInteraction: Animate deterministic state, chart, and shared-element changes from explicit start and end layouts; preserve readable holds and deliberate cuts or impacts. For interactive HTML, suitable optional patterns include scroll-progress chapter or card reveals, pointer tilt, accessible carousel controls, graph selection, and real map navigation. Reverse and direct seeks must restore coherent states. Video uses composition time, not live input; assign one owner per animated property.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and user requirements. Playback, waveform display, and spatial panning are separate choices; tilt alone does not imply audio. Use authorized assets and verify intelligibility, balance, clipping, and sync.
assetRequirements: Reuse or accurately reconstruct the actual product UI, copy, branding, and supplied assets; use stable fonts and preserve context in crops. Prepare diagrams, charts, or maps only from verified relationships and data. Missing assets and audio availability are unspecified. Keep sources and crop recipes non-destructive; preserve map attribution when applicable.
combinations: Can stand alone for feature demos. Optional support: style-093 headline cards between UI states, using product typography and quieter motion; or style-109 line diagrams for real integrations, with card → connector → state-change sequencing and no decorative links. Other patterns are conditional on scene content and must not invent UI or relationships.
productionApproach: Choose renderer and motion engine for style and action first; SVG/DOM may suffice, with graph or map libraries only for real data and interactions. Use HyperFrames for composition, seekable timing, sync, validation, and export; Remotion only if unavailable or a verified requirement cannot be met, recording why. Keep visuals and motion in their own layers. Load assets and fonts, drive video from shared seekable time, and inspect representative frames and decoded output.
